text:
alex: Heads-up - Prospect 'FirstTrust Bank' asked for an ISMS applicability note for the proof-of-concept. They specifically want: scope boundaries, any control exclusions for the POC, and who holds crypto keys during the trial. Can security + solutions help craft a short reply?

sarah: Can you paste their email so we don't misquote them?
alex: Quote from Bank sec: 
> 'For the POC please provide a concise ISMS applicability statement (one page max). We need: 1) which ISO27001 controls/processes apply to the POC; 2) explicit exclusions; 3) key management model and who is responsible for key custody; 4) whether any subcontractors are in-scope.'

pranav: Important detail: this POC will run on a dedicated cluster we provision in our cloud account for them, not our public multi-tenant API. That affects control ownership for network and infra.
katie: Our standard deliverable for these asks is a single-page applicability + a 2-column ownership table (Redwood vs Customer) and a short cover email. Should confirm if they want a signed attestation or just documentation.

sarah: Drafting quick points: 
- Scope: Redwood Inference services used for FirstTrust POC (dedicated GPU cluster + control plane services enabling the cluster). Applies: asset management, access control, cryptography, incident response, change mgmt for the provisioned resources.
- Exclusions: Redwood public hosted model catalog, training pipelines, and optional telemetry that FirstTrust opts out of. Physical data center controls for cloud provider are not in Redwood's direct scope (see subprocessor list).
- Key custody: Default: Redwood-managed KMS for test keys during POC. BYOK/HSM available if customer requests; we document shared responsibilities in the matrix.

alex: Add brief note on logging: operational logs are kept for the POC but we can redact sensitive fields and shorten retention on request. Also note that tenant data used for inference remains customer data.

pranav: For Private/on-prem installs we mark more controls as customer responsibility (physical security, host hardening, local KMS). We'll call that out so they understand differences.
katie: I'll pull the current subprocessor list and latest ISO cert to attach. Also recommend we include pointers to evidence: ISO27001 certificate, SOC snapshot, and screenshots for RBAC config.

sarah: If they ask for signed evidence (signed applicability or attestation) we escalate to compliance/legal; that usually takes ~7-14 calendar days. Otherwise we can send the doc today.

alex: Timeline: they asked for this by COB tomorrow. Can security + solutions get a 1-pager + matrix + short email draft by EOD today?

pranav: I'll assemble the matrix (identity/access, crypto, network, logging, change mgmt, incident response) and mark each as Redwood / Customer / Shared with evidence links. ETA 3 hours.
katie: I'll prepare the cover email. Suggested line: "Attached is our ISMS applicability statement for the POC; this is documentation-only unless a signed attestation is requested."

security-bot: Reminder: attach subprocessor_list_v2026-03.pdf and iso27001_cert_2025.pdf when sending.

alex: Great. Once we have drafts I'll post them here and then send to FirstTrust sec and cc legal. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

pranav: Small clarifier for keys: For Redwood-managed keys we store keys in our KMS and manage rotation. For BYOK, customer provisions keys into their KMS and we never export private material. I'll include that exact phrasing in the doc.
sarah: Perfect. I'll integrate and upload the draft in ~2.5 hrs.
